analysis.title: Jensen Job Loss Jolts Big-Tech; Bitcoin, Bonds, & Bullion Battered But Brent Bid
key_insights: Jensen Huang resigned from NVDA on 11/12 after further revelations the prior night. NVDA dropped sharply at the open, retail dip-buyers pushed stocks into the green, then the gains faded and stocks closed red. NVDA ended down about 4-5%.
NVDA is at its lowest since July 2025, about 35% below its highs, and fell below a $4 trillion market cap.

The DoJ is probing Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect of possible spying, over whether entities linked to her were involved in smuggling Super Micro Computer (SMCI) products to China. SMCI shares fell.

Index action: RTY (most rate-sensitive) fell the most, and the other majors closed down about 0.5%. SPX briefly regained its 100DMA, then failed. The 'most shorted' basket and Goldman's Retail Favorites basket rallied early and faded.

Money moved within the AI trade rather than leaving it. AMD and AVGO gains nearly offset the NVDA drop, and NVDA was the single heaviest SPX weight. NeoClouds were hit hardest, while Semis and Data Centers were hit least.
Sector dispersion shows capital rotating out of high-beta growth and AI-adjacent names into defensive and commodity-linked sectors, with index-level damage contained.
Credit was unfazed. IG spreads, hyperscaler spreads and Data-Center CDS spreads tightened. Energy credit also tightened as energy stocks outperformed.

Oil rose after Trump said the US could forgo a deal with Iran, and Iran's Army said two oil tankers struck mines east of the Strait of Hormuz. A bearish DOE supply report gave only a brief offset. WTI closed above the prior day's highs at $89.
US and EU natural gas rallied on cold weather forecasts and faster storage drawdowns. US futures rose independently of crude because production dipped as producers held back supply until prices rise.

Treasury yields rose 12-13bps on the day (the long end rose 8bps) on sticky CPI from the prior day, hawkish Fed speakers and higher oil. An ugly 30Y auction added to the selloff, and the 10Y yield is back above 5.10%.

Rate-hike odds rose: 15% chance of a 50bps hike in December and 75% chance of a January hike. Cleveland Fed's Hammack, who dissented in favor of a hike last month, said policy needs a restrictive stance.
The 10-year TIPS yield is up 90bps year-to-date and heading for a fifth straight daily rise. This points to real tightening expectations, not only higher breakevens.
The dollar extended out of its 18-month range. Gold fell sharply on rising real yields, and Bitcoin fell to its lowest since August.

BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky said SOXX has returned to the area (~$155) where he advised reducing risk. SOXX is at its 200 DMA with six months of overhead supply. He sees a possible fill of the October gap near $169 but little upside beyond it. A close above $175 would make him rethink.

Goldman's Chris Hussey cites Steve Jobs's 2011 medical leave as an analog. Apple's NTM P/E fell from ~17X to ~12X over the prior ~18 months, hit ~9X in 2013, then recovered to ~15X. The note says the analogy overstates key-person risk and understates structural factors.

risk_factors: Escalation around the Strait of Hormuz and a US-Iran deal falling through, which would push oil and inflation expectations higher.
Sticky inflation and further Fed rate hikes, with rising real yields.
Key-person and governance risk at NVDA, the heaviest SPX weight, with a possible spillover to AI names.
Weak Treasury auction demand, as seen in the 30Y auction.
A dollar breakout from its 18-month range pressuring gold and crypto.
vol_and_positioning: The 'most shorted' basket and Goldman's Retail Favorites basket rallied early on retail dip-buying and faded, a sign the short-squeeze demand ran out.
SOXX has six months of overhead supply from buyers who are now underwater, and it sits at its 200 DMA.
geopolitical: Trump said the US could forgo a deal with Iran: 'We don't need a deal with Iran... we've got their strait!' This dims prospects of ending the war that has disrupted Middle East supply.
Iran's Army said two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz.
The DoJ is probing Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect of possible spying, over alleged smuggling of Super Micro products to China.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Chris Hussey offers the Steve Jobs analog; the note says it overstates key-person risk and understates structural factors.

tension_points.bull_case: Money rotated within the AI trade, and AMD and AVGO gains nearly offset NVDA's drop. Commentators argue the AI business will keep expanding across players.
tension_points.bear_case: BTIG sees a confirmed six-month top for semis, with the 200 DMA and overhead supply limiting upside, and a CEO-less sector leader.
